also: he was not his usual self

terms.gloss: self, one’s very self (with the reflexive: sē ipsum, tē ipsum)
evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.67: nisi aequē amīcōs et nōsmet ipsōs dīligāmus (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 1.2.33: ut tē ipsum servēs
terms.comment: English “self” is a pronoun in Latin: the reflexive strengthened with ipse: tē ipsum, yourself; nōsmet ipsōs, ourselves (see oneself, myself, himself).

terms.grammar: the genitive of the reflexive, after a noun
evidence: Hor. C. 1.18.14: caecus amor suī (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 25.37.12: tanta fīdūcia suī (Lewis & Short, s.v. fīdūcia)
Sen. Ben. 2.26.1: nēmō nōn benignus est suī jūdex (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: English compounds in self- are made with suī: amor suī, self-love; fīdūcia suī, self-confidence (Livy; Traupman 157 gives fīdūcia alone); suī jūdex, judge in one’s own case. For self-control see control.

terms.gloss: (being) one’s usual self, true to form
terms.grammar: similis with the genitive of the reflexive
evidence: Ter. Ph. 3.2.16: quam uterque est similis suī! (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Like himself”: just as he always is.

terms.gloss: to be oneself, in one’s right mind; nōn sum apud mē, I am not myself
evidence: Ter. Hec. 4.4.85: Num tibi vidētur esse apud sēsē? (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Haut. 5.1.48: prae īrācundiā, Menedēme, nōn sum apud mē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “to be at home with oneself”. Mostly negative or with vix: not oneself, beside oneself with anger, fear or joy (Lewis & Short, s.v. apud).

phrases.latin: cum igitur ‘nōsce tē’ dīcit, hoc dīcit: ‘nōsce animum tuum’
phrases.english: so when he says “know yourself”, he means “know your soul”
how like himself each of them is!

phrases.latin: Num tibi vidētur esse apud sēsē?
phrases.english: Does he seem to you to be himself?

phrases.latin: Vix sum apud mē: ita animus commōtust metū, spē, gaudiō.
phrases.english: I am hardly myself, my mind is so shaken by fear, hope and joy.
He was not his usual self.

sources: Lewis & Short: ipse · Lewis & Short: sui · Lewis & Short: similis · Lewis & Short: apud · Lewis & Short: fiducia · Lewis & Short: nosco
